description: Labelled retrieval corpus for OMERO. A fictional company, Halden Systems. Documents include deliberate near-miss distractors (two vendor renewals, two budgets, similar incident reports). Each question names its relevant document(s) and a fact phrase that a correct citation snippet must contain. Type 'paraphrase' asks in different words; 'keyword' hinges on an exact name, code or figure.

documents.title: Board minutes, Q3 2026
documents.text: The board met on 14 October 2026. Revenue for the third quarter grew 18 percent year on year, driven by enterprise subscriptions in the logistics segment. The board approved the FY2027 hiring plan of 42 new roles, weighted towards engineering and customer support. A proposal to open a Singapore office was deferred to the January meeting pending a tax review. The chair noted that gross margin held at 71 percent despite higher hosting costs.

documents.title: Board minutes, Q2 2026
documents.text: The board met on 9 July 2026. Second quarter revenue grew 11 percent, below the 15 percent target, because two large logistics renewals slipped into July. The board asked management to tighten the forecasting process. The audit committee reported no material weaknesses. Approval of the FY2027 hiring plan was postponed until the third quarter results were known.

documents.title: FY2027 budget summary
documents.text: The FY2027 operating budget is 31.5 million dollars. Engineering receives 12.2 million, sales and marketing 9.8 million, customer support 4.1 million, and general and administrative 5.4 million. Cloud hosting is budgeted at 2.6 million, up from 2.1 million, reflecting growth in data volumes. A contingency reserve of 0.8 million is held by the finance director.

documents.title: FY2026 budget summary
documents.text: The FY2026 operating budget was 26.0 million dollars. Engineering received 10.1 million and sales and marketing 8.2 million. Cloud hosting was budgeted at 2.1 million. Travel was cut by 30 percent compared with the previous year after the move to remote-first working.

documents.title: Nimbus Cloud contract renewal
documents.text: Our hosting contract with Nimbus Cloud renews on 1 March 2027 for a three-year term. The negotiated rate is 0.021 dollars per gigabyte-hour with a committed spend of 2.4 million dollars over the term. Termination requires 90 days written notice. The contract owner is Priya Shah in infrastructure. Key risk: the committed spend locks us in if data volumes fall.

documents.title: Brightline HR software renewal
documents.text: The Brightline HR platform subscription renews on 1 June 2027 for one year at 86,000 dollars. Brightline handles payroll, leave and onboarding for all staff. People operations wants to evaluate two alternatives before renewal because the onboarding module is slow. Termination requires 30 days notice.

documents.title: Incident report INC-2041
documents.text: INC-2041: on 3 September 2026 the document ingestion service stopped processing uploads for 47 minutes. The root cause was an expired TLS certificate on the internal message queue. Uploads were queued and none were lost. Corrective action: certificate expiry is now monitored with alerts 30 days ahead, owned by the platform team.

documents.title: Incident report INC-2077
documents.text: INC-2077: on 22 September 2026 search results were slow for about two hours, with the 95th percentile latency reaching 4.8 seconds. The cause was a missing index after a schema migration. The index was rebuilt and a migration check was added to the release pipeline. No data was affected.

documents.title: Information security policy
documents.text: All staff laptops use full-disk encryption and automatic screen lock after five minutes. Production access requires hardware security keys and is reviewed quarterly by the security lead. Customer data is never copied to personal devices. Suspected security incidents must be reported to security@halden.example within one hour of discovery.

documents.title: Password and account policy
documents.text: Passwords must be at least 14 characters. Accounts lock for 15 minutes after ten failed sign-in attempts. Multi-factor authentication is mandatory for email, the code repository and the finance system. Shared accounts are not permitted; service accounts are owned by a named engineer.

documents.title: Remote work guidelines
documents.text: Halden is remote-first. Teams overlap for at least four hours a day in their main time zone. Each employee receives a home office allowance of 1,200 dollars on joining and 300 dollars a year after that. Teams meet in person twice a year; travel is booked through the finance team.

documents.title: Travel and expense policy
documents.text: Economy class is the default for flights under six hours. Hotel spend is capped at 220 dollars a night outside major cities and 320 dollars in London, New York and Singapore. Receipts must be submitted within 30 days. Client entertainment above 500 dollars needs approval from a director.

documents.title: Engineering onboarding checklist
documents.text: In week one a new engineer sets up their laptop, gets repository access and ships a small change to production with a buddy. In week two they join the on-call shadow rotation. By the end of the first month they should have reviewed at least ten pull requests and written one design note.

documents.title: On-call rotation and escalation
documents.text: The platform on-call rotation is one week long and hands over on Mondays at 10:00 UTC. A page must be acknowledged within 10 minutes. If the primary does not respond, the page escalates to the secondary and then to the engineering manager after 20 minutes. On-call engineers receive a stipend of 400 dollars per week.

documents.title: Product roadmap 2027
documents.text: The 2027 roadmap has three themes. First, audio and video research: transcripts searchable with timestamps by the second quarter. Second, project workspaces with shared findings and reports. Third, an admin console for usage and billing. The roadmap explicitly excludes an on-premise version in 2027.

documents.title: Pricing change proposal
documents.text: Product proposes raising the Pro plan from 49 to 59 dollars per user per month from 1 April 2027, with existing customers keeping the old price for twelve months. Modelling suggests churn would rise by under one percentage point. Sales asked for a discount band for teams above 50 seats.

documents.title: Account review: Acme Freight
documents.text: Acme Freight is our largest logistics customer, with 640 seats and an annual contract value of 410,000 dollars. Their main request is faster ingestion of scanned delivery notes. Renewal is due in November 2026. The account owner is Daniel Okafor. Risk: their new CTO is evaluating a competitor.

documents.title: Account review: Veldt Logistics
documents.text: Veldt Logistics has 120 seats and an annual contract value of 74,000 dollars. They use OMERO mainly for audit preparation. Satisfaction is high and they asked about single sign-on. Renewal is due in February 2027. The account owner is Mei Tanaka.

documents.title: FY2027 hiring plan detail
documents.text: Of the 42 approved roles, 24 are in engineering, 8 in customer support, 6 in sales and 4 in operations. Hiring is front-loaded: 60 percent of offers should be accepted by the end of the second quarter. The recruiting budget, including agency fees, is 1.1 million dollars. Each hiring manager owns a quarterly target.

documents.title: Data retention schedule
documents.text: Customer documents are kept for as long as the customer's contract is active and deleted within 30 days of termination. Application logs are kept for 90 days. Backups are encrypted and kept for 35 days. Audit events are kept for one year. Legal hold requests go to the general counsel.

documents.title: Backup and disaster recovery plan
documents.text: The primary database is backed up continuously with point-in-time recovery for 7 days. The recovery point objective is 15 minutes and the recovery time objective is 4 hours. A full restore drill runs every quarter; the last drill in August 2026 restored production data into a staging environment in 2 hours 40 minutes.

documents.title: Architecture overview
documents.text: The product is a Next.js frontend talking to a Python FastAPI service. Documents are stored in object storage and their chunks and embeddings in Postgres with the pgvector extension. Ingestion jobs are recorded in Postgres and processed by worker threads. Answers are generated by a hosted language model and fall back to quoted extracts when no model is available.

documents.title: AI model usage policy
documents.text: Only approved model providers may process customer content, and only under agreements that forbid training on our data. Prompts and outputs containing customer data must not be logged in third-party tools. Every generated answer must cite the internal source it is based on, and answers without evidence must say so.

documents.title: Sales report, Q3 2026
documents.text: New bookings in Q3 were 2.9 million dollars against a target of 2.5 million. The logistics vertical contributed 58 percent of bookings. Average deal size rose to 38,000 dollars. The sales cycle shortened from 74 to 61 days after the introduction of a guided trial. Two deals above 200,000 dollars closed in the final week.

documents.title: Customer support metrics, Q3 2026
documents.text: The support team resolved 3,410 tickets in the third quarter. Median first response time was 38 minutes and customer satisfaction was 94 percent. The most common topic was document upload failures, at 22 percent of tickets, followed by billing questions at 15 percent.

documents.title: Singapore office tax review
documents.text: Opening a Singapore entity would let us hire in the region and serve Asian logistics customers locally. The tax review estimates setup costs of 180,000 dollars and an effective tax rate of 17 percent. The review recommends waiting until regional revenue exceeds 3 million dollars a year.

documents.title: Engineering objectives, Q4 2026
documents.text: Objective one: make ingestion durable, so no upload is lost on restart. Objective two: cut 95th percentile search latency below 800 milliseconds. Objective three: reach 80 percent automated test coverage on the API. Each objective has a named owner and is reviewed every two weeks.

documents.title: Annual vendor review
documents.text: Finance reviewed 23 software vendors this year. Total software spend was 1.9 million dollars. Four tools with overlapping features were cancelled, saving 140,000 dollars a year. The largest contract remains cloud hosting. Every vendor handling customer data must pass a security questionnaire before renewal.

documents.title: All-hands notes, September 2026
documents.text: The CEO thanked the team for a record quarter. Project workspaces will launch to all customers in November. The company will close between 24 December and 1 January. Questions from staff focused on the hiring plan and on whether the Singapore office would go ahead, which remains undecided.

documents.title: Transcript: platform stand-up, 12 October
documents.text: Priya: the certificate monitoring from the September incident is live. Tomas: I'm still chasing the slow search queries, I think the reranker adds about 300 milliseconds. Priya: let's put the reranker behind a setting until we have measurements. Tomas: agreed, I'll have numbers by Friday.

documents.title: Data processing agreement template
documents.text: Under our standard data processing agreement Halden acts as processor and the customer as controller. Sub-processors are listed on our website and customers receive 30 days notice of changes. Personal data breaches are notified to the customer without undue delay and in any case within 48 hours.

documents.title: Learning and development budget
documents.text: Each employee has a learning budget of 1,500 dollars a year for courses, books and conferences. Unused budget does not roll over. Conference travel counts against the budget. Managers approve requests above 500 dollars.
